title: Volatility targeting (managed volatility)
source: Alpha Architect; Fin. Analysts Journal 'Conditional Volatility Targeting' (2020)
summary: Size positions inversely to recent realized volatility to hold roughly constant risk; shrink exposure when markets turn turbulent, expand when calm. Cut S&P500 drawdown from -37% to -21% in 2008; improves risk-adjusted ratios 15-50%.
application: Bear-market crashes (2018, 2022 — our exact open problem) spike realized vol. Added a causal per-symbol vol-ratio channel (recent/typical std of log returns) in infer.py; brain scales each position by clamp(1/vol_ratio, floor, cap). Long-only compatible: it only reduces/mildly grows size, never shorts. Testing OFF vs cap 1.3/1.6 on the champion's per-year grid.
result: Offline on the champion net: cap 1.3x lifts the worst year -16.7%->-14.7% (+2.0pp) and score -0.1534->-0.1359; cap 1.6 hurts 2018. Baseline OFF reproduces the champion exactly. Folded into the loop's risk grid (optional 5th column = vol_scale). Moves the floor the right way; not all-positive alone yet. In-loop update (iter with vol grid): the SELECTED config for a new net was vol-OFF (score -0.1387, worst -14.4%) — vol 1.3 did not win that particular net (ledger logs only the winning config, not all 6, so inconclusive; effect is net-dependent). Kept in the grid as a competing option; controlled offline gain stands. WON IN-LOOP (2026-08-20): a new champion promoted with vol_scale 1.3 — score -0.1179 (was -0.1534), worst year -13.3% (was -16.7%), and 2022 -16.7%->-3.6% (near-flat in the bear year, exactly vol targeting's job). Vol targeting is now part of the champion. CAVEAT: this champion's SEALED 2026 readout is -0.8% (old champion was +22%) — better on the per-year law but a worse forward readout; the sealed window is doing its job of warning about generalization. Not selected on, just noted.

title: Triple-barrier labeling
source: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial ML; Hudson & Thames; QuantStrategy.io
summary: Replace fixed-horizon labels with three volatility-scaled barriers: upper (take-profit), lower (stop), vertical (time). Label = which barrier the path hits first. Labels adapt to volatility instead of a fixed threshold.
application: Our oracle currently labels a buy-point by a fixed threshold move over a horizon (max-ops idea). Triple-barrier would make the target volatility-aware and align the label with how we actually exit (we already have stop_loss + trail_stop + min_hold). Could raise the net's precision and cut the toll. Needs a change in pooled.py label construction; retrain required. A/B vs current labels on per-year score.

title: Meta-labeling (separate side from size)
source: Lopez de Prado (2017/2018); Hudson & Thames 'Does Meta-Labeling add to signal efficacy?'
summary: A primary model decides direction (side); a secondary model decides whether to act and how big (size), trained on the primary's true/false positives. Cuts false positives and optimizes sizing without retraining the primary.
application: Our TCN is the primary 'side' model. A meta-model over (prob, trend, vol, regime) that predicts whether an entry will be a winner would filter low-quality entries — directly attacking our churn/toll problem and lifting precision in choppy bear years. Fits our risk layer as a learned gate on top of the enter band. Build as a small classifier on the loop's own labeled entries.

title: Cross-sectional momentum ranking + trend overlay
source: Drogen/Hoffstein/Otte (SSRN 2023); arXiv:2512.08124 'Long-only crypto portfolio by ranking assets: a NN approach'
summary: Rank the universe by relative strength (e.g., 30d) and hold the strongest; a trend-following overlay took a long-only crypto book's max drawdown from 75% to 45% while raising returns. In broad selloffs, relative strength naturally concentrates into few/no names.
application: SPEC after reading arXiv:2512.08124 full text. We already hold top-K by prob among uptrend names; add a cross-sectional RANK among the entry candidates by relative strength (e.g., trailing 30d/80d return, or Sharpe) and (a) prefer the top-ranked, and/or (b) size by rank^2 (the paper's best weighting, Sharpe 1.01). Implement as a per-symbol momentum channel in infer.py ({symbol}__mom) + a rank gate/sizer in the brain, no retrain, off by default. IMPORTANT caveat from the paper: cross-sectional ranking ALONE had 77% max drawdown and 'drops at the end of the bearish market' — it is a SELECTION/SIZING refinement, NOT a bear defense. Our trend filter + vol targeting + 25% mandate supply the defense the paper lacks; rank^2 sizing rides on top to concentrate on relative winners. A/B on per-year score; expect help in choppy/mixed years more than in 2018/2022.
result: REJECTED (this form). Offline on the champion, the cross-sectional mom_gate HURT: gate 0.5 -> score -0.1613 worst -17.3%; gate 0.7 -> score -0.1662 worst -17.6% (baseline OFF -0.1534 / -16.7%). It concentrates into 'relative winners' that still crash in 2022 and drops good absolute entries our trend+prob filter already picks well — matches the paper's caveat (ranking alone had 77% DD). Code kept dormant (off by default), NOT wired to the loop. UNTESTED variant left for later: rank^2-weighted SIZING among the already-selected top-K (the paper's actual best lever), rather than a gate that removes names.

title: Sample-uniqueness / return-attribution weighting
source: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial ML (ch. 4)
summary: Overlapping labels make training samples non-IID; weighting each sample by its uniqueness (how few other labels overlap it) and by return attribution reduces overfitting to redundant windows.
application: Our windows overlap heavily (a label every bar over 15m data), so the net over-weights redundant, correlated examples — a plausible source of the overfitting we fought. Add per-sample weights in train.py's loss (BCE with weight). No new data; a training-only change. A/B on val generalization + per-year score.
result: APPLIED — big consistency win (2026-08-20). Adapted honestly: our labels are per-bar hold/flat STATES (oracle.py zigzag), NOT triple-barrier forward-horizon events, so concurrency c_t doesn't map — instead the redundancy is a swing's DURATION (a 500-bar hold-run = ~500 near-identical examples of one swing). train._uniqueness_weights sets each bar's weight = 1/(contiguous-run length) per symbol block, normalised to mean 1, so every oracle swing contributes equal weight; applied to BCEWithLogitsLoss(reduction='none'). Wired as searchable flag uniqueness_weighting[0,1] in search.json; loop A/B-tests on/off. Watching whether it lifts the worst year AND improves the champion's sealed 2026 readout (the generalization gap it targets). Also narrowed trend_span to 30/60d (90/120d confirmed worse over 3+ iters). Weighted-loss path validated in isolation (finite loss + clean backward, matches train.py inner loop); CONTROLLED A/B in-loop (same trend_span 2880 / window 128 / vol 1.3): uniq=1 -> score -0.091 worst -10.4% cagr +12.9%; uniq=0 -> score -0.1557 worst -16.1% cagr +5%. Worst year +5.7pp, and PROMOTED to champion (now score -0.091, worst -10.4%, 2018 -6.2% and 2025 +1.7% both much better — evenly improved, as expected when the net stops over-fitting long trends). CAVEAT: the specific generalization hypothesis (better sealed 2026) is NOT confirmed — 2026 stayed ~flat (-0.8% -> -1.3%). So uniqueness is a strong IN-SAMPLE consistency lever that did not hurt the sealed readout, but did not close the forward gap either. Now stacked with vol-targeting in the champion.

title: Fractional differentiation of features
source: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial ML (ch. 5)
summary: Fractionally-differentiate price series to make them stationary while PRESERVING memory (integer differencing throws memory away). Keeps predictive signal that full returns destroy.
application: Some of our features may be near-non-stationary or over-differenced. A frac-diff transform of price-derived features could retain long memory the TCN can use for regime awareness. Add as an optional feature transform in features.py; retrain; compare val accuracy + per-year score.

title: Purged & embargoed validation split
source: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial ML (ch. 7)
summary: In financial ML, train and validation windows that touch overlapping label horizons leak. Purge overlapping samples and embargo a gap between train and val to get an honest generalization estimate.
application: Our val is each symbol's recent slice. pooled.py already leaves a +window gap, but the zigzag oracle labels are computed over the WHOLE series, so train bars near the split can leak post-split info via pivots — likely inflating our val-based band/risk selection and contributing to the sealed-2026 gap (which vol/uniqueness did not close). SPEC: in pooled.py build_pooled, add an `embargo` (bars) so va = ends[split + window + embargo:] and drop train ends within `embargo` of the split; expose as a searchable flag (embargo bars, e.g. 0 vs ~288=3d vs ~960=10d). Complementary — does NOT touch the oracle or the brain. A/B on whether it narrows the val-vs-2026 gap (compare a promoted net's sealed 2026 with vs without embargo). NEXT to implement.
result: IMPLEMENTED + A/B-TESTING IN THE LOOP (2026-08-20). pooled.build_pooled gained an `embargo` param: tr=ends[:split-embargo] (purge leaky boundary train samples), va=ends[split+window+embargo:] (embargo the val start). Threaded through train.train and autoloop; searchable flag embargo[0,288,960] in search.json (0/3d/10d). Backward-compatible (embargo=0 = prior). Loop restarted; first iteration already trained with embargo=960 without error. Verdict pending: watching whether embargo>0 nets narrow the val-vs-sealed-2026 gap (need a promoted embargo net to read its 2026). VAL-WINDOWS CHECK (2026-08-20): embargo=960 leaves val_windows=584787 = 19.7% effective val fraction over 2.97M pooled windows (train 2.39M) — the split is NOT broken; embargo drops only ~13k boundary windows (~0.4%), negligible. But a duplicate-loop bug (two autoloops racing on the same files, from a nohup relaunch that survived when I thought it died) kept restarting the loop mid-iteration, so EVERY prior embargo>0 iteration was killed before completing: the ledger still has 0 completed embargo>0 records (14 records, all embargo 0/None). Fixed the duplicate (single loop pid 3484); the running iter (embargo=960, uniq=1, 30d, epoch 27/50) will be the FIRST embargo>0 ledger row. Verdict still pending on real data. VERDICT — REJECTED as a search dimension (2026-08-20). First (and only) completed embargo>0 net: embargo=960, uniq=1, 30d -> score -0.0959, worst year -11.0% (2022), NO promotion so no sealed-2026 readout. Same-params embargo=0 baseline (the champion, uniq=1/30d) -> score -0.091, worst -10.4%. So embargo=960 is WORSE on the selection metric AND on the binding year 2022 (-11.0% vs -10.4%) — the year embargo needed to help, it didn't. Its per-year profile is mixed (2018 +0.75% vs champion -6.2%), but that 2018 lift is CONFOUNDED: the embargo net's risk sweep dropped vol_scale (had vol1.3 available, didn't pick it), and vol targeting is what depresses the champion's 2018 — so the 2018 gain is the missing-vol effect, not embargo. DECISIVE reason (structure, not n): embargo LOWERS the validation selection score, so embargo nets never promote, so the sealed-2026-gap hypothesis it was BUILT to test is unfalsifiable through the loop — a lever that cannot demonstrate its own benefit and mildly hurts the binding year does not earn 2/3 of the search budget on a plateau. Reverted search.json embargo->[0]. Code kept dormant + backward-compatible (embargo param works, embargo=0 = prior behaviour), reusable if a dedicated 2026-gap eval that does NOT route through promotion is ever built. Consistent with the ensemble rejection (real but too small/structurally-blocked to pay for).

title: Ensemble / bagged nets for year-to-year consistency
source: Lopez de Prado (bagging in finance); general ML variance reduction
summary: Averaging several nets trained on bootstrapped/seed-varied samples reduces variance — the enemy of consistency. A committee is steadier across regimes than any single net.
application: Our objective is literally low variance across calendar years, and the sealed-2026 gap (which uniqueness did NOT close) is a generalization problem — bagging attacks BOTH. SPEC: add an `ensemble` param; train N seed-varied nets (same cfg, different seeds; optionally bootstrap-subsample train_ends), save N weight files; in infer.export load all N and average their sigmoid probs BEFORE the band. A/B ensemble 1 vs 3 via search.json. Cost: N x train time (~40min -> ~120min at N=3) — sample N=3 rarely, or make it a small fixed 2-3. Priority raised to HIGH: it is the top remaining lever for the 2026 generalization gap and for lifting the worst year by damping single-net regime luck. NEXT to implement.
result: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20 (backward-compatible, ensemble=1 = current). train.py trains N seed-varied nets (oracle_net.pt + oracle_net_1.pt ...), averages their val probs for band selection; infer.export globs all oracle_net*.pt and averages sigmoid probs before the band; _promote copies/clears all members; searchable flag ensemble[1,1,3] in search.json (weighted to 1 to control the N x train cost). All files compile. Minimal end-to-end validation (train ensemble=2 + export) running before enabling in the loop; VALIDATION PASSED (2026-08-20): trained ensemble=2 seed-varied nets (distinct losses 0.5606/0.5598), saved oracle_net.pt+oracle_net_1.pt, band selection on averaged val probs OK, infer.export loaded+averaged both, exit 0. Loop RESTARTED with ensemble active (search ensemble[1,1,3]). Now A/B ensemble 1 vs 3 on the per-year score AND the sealed 2026 (the gap it targets); FIRST ens=3 RESULT (2026-08-20, ~71min/iter): ens=3 (uniq0,vol1.3,30d) score -0.1175 worst -12.8%, and 2018 turned POSITIVE (+2.1%) for the first time. Near-controlled vs the same-config ens=1 (score -0.1557 worst -16.1%): ensemble lifted the worst year +3.3pp — supports the variance-reduction hypothesis. CAVEATS: n=1 (different seeds, not a clean A/B); it did NOT promote (< champion -0.091) so no sealed-2026 readout yet to test generalization; 2022 still -12.8%. A 2nd ens=3 is training. VERDICT after 2 ens=3 (2026-08-20): REJECTED as a blanket setting — benefit is marginal and config-dependent at 3x train cost. Sample A (uniq0,vol1.3,30d): ens=3 worst -12.8% vs ens=1 -16.1% = +3.3pp (2018 flipped +2.1%). Sample B (uniq0,voloff,60d): ens=3 worst -8.9% vs ens=1 -9.1% = +0.2pp, score slightly WORSE. Neither ens=3 promoted, so the sealed-2026 generalization hypothesis stayed untested. Reverted search.json ensemble->[1] to preserve throughput (3x cost not justified broadly). Code kept dormant (ensemble param works, backward-compatible) — could be reused later to bag one specific promising config. Net-net: variance reduction real but too small/inconsistent here to pay for.

title: Market-breadth risk-off gate (flatten when universe participation collapses)
source: Original synthesis for our 14-coin universe, grounded in classic market-breadth risk-off filters (% of members above MA; intalcon, enlightenedstocktrading, protraderdashboard)
summary: An ABSOLUTE regime switch: compute universe breadth = fraction of the 14 coins currently in a causal uptrend (reusing the existing per-symbol __trend bit). When breadth falls below a threshold K, the whole book goes to cash (flatten + block entries) — the market-wide participation has collapsed, so even lone bounces are not to be trusted. Classic breadth work: >50% supports longs, persistent <~40% = narrow rallies prone to failure.
application: Directly targets 2022 — THE binding year that vol, uniqueness, ensemble and embargo all failed to fix (2022 is a broad grinding bear where the per-symbol trend filter still admits temporary bounces). DISTINCT from the REJECTED cross-sectional momentum gate: that reranked names by RELATIVE strength (and still crashed in 2022); this is an ABSOLUTE de-risk of the entire book based on universe participation. Implemented in strategy.py brain: new param breadth_gate (0=off); each bar breadth = (#coins with trend=1)/(#coins with a trend map among those trading); if breadth < breadth_gate -> risk_off: force-exit held names (like a soft stop, overriding min_hold) and take no new entries. No retrain, no new infer channel (reuses __trend). Backward-compatible: breadth_gate=0 or no trend maps -> off. Wired as an optional 6th element of the risk-grid rows (after vol_scale) so the per-year sweep A/B-tests it OFF vs K in {0.30,0.35}. Expect: 2022 (and 2018) exposure cut hard in the broad-bear stretches, lifting the WORST year without touching bull years where breadth stays high.
result: IMPLEMENTED + WIRED (2026-08-20): strategy.py breadth_gate (force-exit RISKOFF + block entries when universe uptrend fraction < K), unit-tested (blocks in-uptrend entries, emits SELL/RISKOFF, gate=0=off), added as optional 6th risk-grid element (breadth 0.30/0.35 on the vol1.3 family). VERDICT LEANS REJECTED, kept testing on more nets. CORRECTION: the offline harness is actually FAITHFUL (I re-exported from the on-disk weights and reproduced the A/B EXACTLY — the apparent '3x under-exposure' was an ARTIFACT of comparing to a CORRUPTED best.json that describes a DIFFERENT, lost net 'B' worst -10.4%; the real on-disk champion 'net A' is worst -4.8%, and my A/B faithfully tested net A). So the A/B is valid ON NET A: breadth cuts 2022 (-4.8->-3.1) but drags 2018 (-4.4->-6.3) and trims every year, making 2018 the new WORST -> worst-year WORSE (-4.8->-6.3) = REJECT on net A. CAVEAT: the verdict depends on the net's 2018-vs-2022 gap (on a net where 2022 dominates the worst-year by a wide margin, cutting 2022 could still help). Also breadth 0.30/0.35/0.40 were IDENTICAL (14 correlated coins -> near-bimodal breadth, little tunable resolution). In that compressed offline regime 2018 (-4.4%) and 2022 (-4.8%) are near-tied so breadth (which cuts 2022 -4.8->-3.1 but drags 2018 -4.4->-6.3 and trims all years) made 2018 the new worst -> looked WORSE. BUT scaling those RELATIVE effects to the TRUE regime (2022 -10.4% dominates, 2018 -6.2%) flips the conclusion: ~35% cut to 2022 -> ~-6.8%, ~43% worse 2018 -> ~-8.9% => worst-year IMPROVES -10.4->-8.9. So the verdict genuinely depends on the true regime the offline harness can't reproduce. Also breadth 0.30/0.35/0.40 were IDENTICAL offline -> on 14 correlated coins breadth is near-bimodal (0 or 1), little tunable resolution. ROOT FIX for the recurring blind spot (ledger logged only the WINNING risk config, so vol AND breadth were un-observable): added record['sweep'] = every risk config's per-year (autoloop _select_risk_years now returns the full sweep). Loop restarted with it. FINAL VERDICT — REJECTED (2026-08-20) on FAITHFUL loop sweep data (record['sweep'], iter1 net uniq1/30d): matched pair mp2/pf0.15/vol1.3 -> no-gate score -0.1382 (2022 -7.0%, 2024 +16%, 2025 +3%) vs +BR0.35 -0.1298 (2022 -6.1% GOOD but 2024 +0%, 2025 -12% RUINED) vs +BR0.30 -0.1702 (2025 -16%). Breadth cuts 2022 as designed but the blunt risk-off FLATTENS during 2024/2025 recoveries and craters them; unstable across thresholds; NO breadth config ever wins the sweep (winner is plain base -0.1090). Trades one bad year for two. Reverted risk_grid.json to the 6 base/vol rows; code kept dormant (breadth_gate=0=off). Lesson: on a small, highly-correlated crypto universe, universe breadth is near-binary and too coarse to be a good regime gate. 2022 stays open for a future idea (asymmetric re-entry, or a per-name absolute-drawdown regime rather than a universe on/off switch).
